edges.mechanism: Antiplatelet activity of AGE could add to anticoagulation; garlic case reports describe enhanced warfarin/fluindione effect. AGE itself did not increase bleeding in a warfarin RCT and garlic did not change warfarin PK/INR in healthy subjects.
edges.evidence: Pilot RCT of AGE 5 mL twice daily in 48 warfarin patients (no increased hemorrhage); crossover PK/PD study; case-report review; observational TTR study; low certainty

edges.mechanism: AGE inhibits ADP-induced platelet aggregation and adhesion; additive effect with aspirin/P2Y12 inhibitors plausible. AGE plus cilostazol did not enhance antiplatelet activity in a small study.
edges.evidence: Human platelet studies, small PD interaction study (n=10), SR of 12 garlic RCTs inconsistent; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Pharmacodynamic additive bleeding risk inferred from garlic antiplatelet activity; no interaction studies with DOACs or heparins.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic inference plus perioperative guidance and case-report review; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Duplicate organosulfur exposure: additive antiplatelet effect and stacking of garlic adverse effects (odour, GI upset, allergy, bleeding); no added benefit shown.
edges.evidence: Platelet studies and adverse-effect reviews; no combination trial; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Garlic caplets lowered saquinavir AUC 51% and Cmax 54%, likely via intestinal P-gp induction; ritonavir single-dose PK not significantly changed. Not tested with AGE.
edges.evidence: Healthy-volunteer PK studies (n=10 each) and duodenal biopsy study; moderate certainty for garlic, unknown for AGE

edges.mechanism: Garlic oil reduced CYP2E1 activity (chlorzoxazone ratio) by 39% in young and ~22% in elderly subjects; AGE not tested.
edges.evidence: Probe-cocktail phenotyping studies; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Garlic extract did not alter alprazolam (CYP3A4), dextromethorphan (CYP2D6), erythromycin breath test, or simvastatin/pravastatin AUC; interaction unlikely.
edges.evidence: Healthy-volunteer probe studies; moderate certainty of no effect for garlic extracts

edges.mechanism: Garlic extract increased duodenal P-gp expression to 131%, which correlated with reduced saquinavir exposure.
edges.evidence: Single human mechanistic study; low certainty

edges.mechanism: AGE lowers SBP further when added to existing antihypertensive therapy; additive effect.
edges.evidence: Adjunct RCTs in treated uncontrolled hypertension; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Garlic modestly lowers fasting glucose and HbA1c; AGE lowered glucose in a 1-year trial; minor additive effect possible.
edges.evidence: MA of 27 RCTs plus AGE RCT; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Fixed AGE+CoQ10 combination slowed CAC progression, lowered CRP and improved PWV/endothelial function; individual contributions not separable.
edges.evidence: Two RCTs in firefighters; low certainty

edges.mechanism: AGE combined with B6, B12, folic acid and L-arginine lowered homocysteine and slowed CAC progression and adipose-tissue growth.
edges.evidence: RCT (n=65) and secondary analyses; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Vitamin B12 status influenced blood-pressure responsiveness to Kyolic in about 17% of hypertensive patients.
edges.evidence: Secondary finding of one RCT plus review; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Cocoa/cacao and garlic both inhibit platelet aggregation in RCTs; stacking may add to bleeding tendency.
edges.evidence: SR of herb antiplatelet RCTs; interaction not studied directly; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Both inhibit platelet aggregation and are among herbs flagged for perioperative bleeding risk; additive effect plausible.
edges.evidence: SR of herb antiplatelet RCTs and perioperative review; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Antiplatelet activity may increase surgical bleeding; ASA/AANA advise stopping herbal medicines 1-2 weeks before elective surgery.
edges.evidence: Perioperative review and case report of garlic-associated surgical bleeding; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Inhibition of platelet aggregation and adhesion could worsen bleeding tendency.
edges.evidence: Human platelet-function studies and case-report review; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Garlic can cause allergic contact dermatitis, urticaria, angioedema and anaphylaxis.
edges.evidence: Case reports summarized in review; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Insufficient evidence on garlic in pregnancy (one trial, odour more common, no serious harms); no AGE-specific data.
edges.evidence: Cochrane review of one RCT (n=100); very low certainty

edges.mechanism: True physiological inhibition of ADP-, collagen- and epinephrine-induced aggregation and adhesion may alter platelet-function test results.
edges.evidence: Human supplementation studies; low certainty
